title: introduce-chefplate-rag-playbook-local-runner-and-type-bindings
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Adds a minimal 'Chefplate' RAG playbook with a local runner, TypeScript bindings, and telemetry probes for iterative authoring.
description:
Motivation: Create a compact, opinionated RAG playbook template for fast local iteration and authoring. 'Chefplate' is a tiny scaffolding that demonstrates: 1) end-to-end local runs against a seeded index, 2) typesafe tool bindings and TS-friendly playbook schemas, and 3) low-friction telemetry probes to make regressions visible during prompt edits. This targets developer experience engineers and product teams who want a reproducible local authoring loop before onboarding to production Redwood pipelines.

What this PR contains (single continuous description):
- Checklist: [x] minimal playbook schema (YAML + TS types), [x] local-runner (node) with hot-reload dev loop, [x] seeded example index + indexer script, [x] telemetry probes and example dashboards (DevConsole snippet), [x] docs page and quickstart README, [x] CI smoke job + unit tests, [x] small e2e scenario.

High-level commits:
- commit 1: create chefplate template layout and README with usage instructions and example prompts
- commit 2: add local-runner implementation (node/ts), lightweight in-memory vector store shim, and hot-reload dev session loop
- commit 3: add typescript bindings and generated types for playbook schemas; add example tools (http-fetch, file-store)
- commit 4: add seeded-index generator script and small sample data set (~60 documents) for repeatable local plays
- commit 5: add telemetry probes and opt-out flag; add DevConsole snippet to docs
- commit 6: CI workflow and smoke e2e; fix linting issues reported by CI and rerun tests

Changed areas (high level):
- examples/chefplate/README.md - new quickstart and recipes
- examples/chefplate/playbook.yaml - opinionated minimal RAG playbook
- examples/chefplate/src/runner/local-runner.ts - local Node runner with hot-reload loop
- examples/chefplate/src/tools/http-fetch.ts - example tool shim and types
- examples/chefplate/src/indexer/seed-data.ts - small index generator
- examples/chefplate/src/types/playbook.d.ts - generated TS types for playbook schema
- docs/playbooks/chefplate.md - docs site quickstart and DevConsole snippet
- ci/workflows/chefplate-ci.yml - small CI to validate smoke e2e and linting

Review conversation snapshot:
- Diego Ramirez (reviewer): "Nice minimal surface. Two asks: (1) add a telemetry opt-out env var so customers can run offline, (2) reduce sample dataset to <100 docs for CI speed."
- Avery Chen (author): "Added TELEMETRY_OFF env and reduced seed data to 60 docs; also added note in README about offline usage."
- Samira Patel (reviewer): "Runner looks good. Could we split hot-reload into a 'dev' flag to keep the example runner simple for CI? Also asked for a short command example for Windows users."
- Avery Chen: "Splitted flag and added explicit powershell commands to README. Addressed lint nit where promises were not awaited."
- Lena Fischer (approver): "Confirming QA smoke pass on macOS and linux. Approving for merge after squash."

CI and test notes:
- First CI run: lint failed (prettier/tsc), fixed in commit 6.
- Subsequent CI run: unit tests and smoke e2e passed. Rerun required for flaky network mock, fixed with deterministic mock and retry wrapper. Final status: pass.

How to try locally (short):
1) git clone && cd examples/chefplate
2) yarn && yarn seed:index (creates local/seed.json)
3) yarn dev:runner --playbook playbook.yaml --dev (hot-reload)
4) open the built DevConsole snippet or hit /metrics to see telemetry probes (TELEMETRY_OFF=1 disables payloads)

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The in-memory vector shim in local-runner intentionally mirrors production calls but does not depend on external stores to keep onboarding friction low. It's not for scale.
- Type generation is intentionally minimal to keep examples approachable; a full codegen pipeline is left to a follow-up task (ENG-3421 follow-ups).

Security and compliance:
- The example includes a telemetry opt-out and avoids shipping any real PII data. Seed data is synthetic.

Merge outcome: Squash merged to main on 2026-03-05 by Lena Fischer (squash merge). Merge commit: 7a3b9f8c0e2d2c8a1f6a4d9b.

Related items: Linear ENG-3421 tracked the follow-ups for full codegen and CI expansion. PM-1101 captured the product acceptance criteria. Support ticket SUP-88 requested an on-prem friendly quickstart; chefplate addresses that by documenting TELEMETRY_OFF and offline runner notes.

Notes for maintainers:
- If you update playbook schema, regenerate types using scripts/generate-types.sh in examples/chefplate.
- Keep the seeded dataset light to avoid long CI times.

This PR aims to be a small, self-contained pattern that teams can fork to prototype RAG flows locally before migrating to Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments.
